sector_model: ad tech platform (nonfinancial): growth, take rate, margins, FCF after SBC, net cash, dilution; not a bank or REIT model
thesis: The Trade Desk (Nasdaq: TTD) runs a self-service programmatic ad buying platform. Q3 2026 (10-Q and release read): revenue 736.0M (-0.5% y/y), 9M revenue 2,139.9M (+4%), 9M operating income 260.8M (-21.5%), 9M net income 142.4M (-44%) with a 64% Q3 tax rate from stock award detriments; customer retention above 95%; Q4 outlook revenue at least 755M (about -11% versus Q4 2025 of 846.8M) and Adjusted EBITDA at least 280M. TTM (FY2025 + 9M 2026 - 9M 2025): revenue 2,986.7M, net income 329.4M, operating income 517.7M, OCF 1,115.3M, capex plus capitalized software 268.3M, FCF 847.0M, SBC 425.9M so FCF after SBC 421.1M. At the 2026-11-10 close of 15.42 and 472.9M Class A plus Class B shares, market cap is 7.29B: 22.1x TTM net income, FCF yield 11.6% (5.8% after SBC), net cash 1.65B with no debt, EV about 10.9x TTM operating income. The stock rose 15.5% on 11-09 and 3.3% on 11-10 after the report. Question the market is asking: whether a former growth leader is now a share losing, margin compressing ad platform; the price already assumes that, but trailing figures are higher than the near term run rate.
counterthesis: Revenue is now flat to down (Q3 -0.5%, Q4 guide about -11%) and the 4% 9M growth includes 15M non-recurring partner revenue and a shift of costs from revenue reductions into platform operations. Operating income fell 21.5% in 9M and Adjusted EBITDA margin dropped from 39% to 33%, so TTM FCF and earnings overstate the run rate. FCF after SBC is only about 5.8% of market cap because SBC is 14% of TTM revenue. Net income is helped by a longer equipment life (about 7M) and an 18M asset sale gain, and operating cash flow by a 203M working capital inflow (receivables collected, payables paid). The 2026 restructuring cost 44M, 14.4M options were repriced on 2026-10-19 (incremental expense not yet measured), and a CEO performance option was struck at 14.97. Securities class actions over 2023 to 2025 statements and a Delaware reincorporation suit are pending. Competition from Amazon and walled gardens, and net versus gross revenue presentation changes, could keep growth below 10%. The 15% two day rebound leaves little margin for a failed recovery.
invalidation: Q4 revenue below the 755M floor, 2027 growth that stays negative or low single digit, Adjusted EBITDA margin staying under about 33%, retention falling below 95%, FCF after SBC turning negative, or an adverse ruling or large settlement in the securities class action. Conversely, revenue growth returning to double digits would change the thesis to a recovery case.
